Internal Policy Extract: Cancellations, Postponements and Deposit Retention
Reference: HFF-POL-07 (Rev. C)
Owner: Operations Manager
Effective: 1 March 2026
Next review: 1 March 2027

7.1 Scope
This clause applies to all bookings for ceremonies, receptions and private hire made through the venue office, including bookings taken by telephone, email or the online enquiry form.

7.2 Deposits
7.2.1 A non-refundable booking deposit of £1,250.00 is payable within 14 days of the provisional booking being confirmed in writing.
7.2.2 The balance of the hire fee is due no later than 60 days before the event date.
7.2.3 Deposits are held in the client account and are not released to the client until the event has taken place.

7.3 Cancellation by the client
7.3.1 Written notice of cancellation received more than 180 days before the event date entitles the client to a refund of the balance paid, less the booking deposit.
7.3.2 Written notice received between 180 and 91 days before the event date entitles the client to a refund of 50% of the balance paid, less the booking deposit.
7.3.3 Notice received 90 days or fewer before the event date entitles the client to no refund.

7.4 Postponement
7.4.1 A client may move a booking once to a new date within 12 months of the original event date, subject to availability, without penalty, provided that written request is received at least 45 days before the original date.
7.4.2 Any second postponement is treated as a cancellation under clause 7.3.

7.5 Exception: bereavement and medical emergency
7.5.1 Where cancellation arises from the death of the client or an immediate family member, or from a medical emergency certified by a registered medical practitioner, the Operations Manager may waive clause 7.3 in full or in part.
7.5.2 Any waiver under 7.5.1 must be approved in writing, recorded on the booking file, and reported to the Director at the next monthly review.
7.5.3 Waivers are not available for cancellations attributed to change of plans, venue unavailability caused by a supplier, or weather.

7.6 Venue-initiated changes
If the venue cancels or materially alters a booking, the client is entitled to a full refund of all sums paid, including the deposit, within 10 working days.

7. Thresholds and quotations

7.1 Any requirement with an estimated total contract value of £25,000 or more (excluding VAT) must follow the formal tender route in Section 8.

7.2 Requirements with an estimated value of at least £5,000 but below £25,000 require written quotations from a minimum of three suppliers, recorded on Form PF-4 (Quotation Record).

7.3 Estimated value is calculated over the full contract term, including any optional extensions. Requirements must not be divided into separate orders to fall below a threshold.

7.4 Where a requisition is raised with an estimate within £1,000 of a threshold in 7.1 or 7.2, the requester must attach a written cost build-up, and the Head of Procurement Operations must confirm the estimate before a purchase order is issued.

7.5 Exception – sole source. Where only one supplier can meet a specification, the requester may proceed with a single quotation regardless of value, provided Form PF-7 (Sole Source Justification) is signed by the budget holder and countersigned by the evaluation panel chair.

7.6 Exception – emergency. Purchases required to prevent immediate risk to health, safety or building integrity may be placed without quotations. The budget holder must report the purchase to Procurement Services within two working days.

7.7 An evaluation panel shall consist of no fewer than four members, at least 60 per cent of whom must be academic or professional staff from outside the requesting department.

7.8 Quotations received after the closing time stated on the request are not to be considered, unless the requester records a justified delay on Form PF-4 and the panel chair approves its inclusion.

14. Leak allowance assessment

14.1 A leak allowance may be considered where a customer's metered consumption for a billing period exceeds the customer's rolling twelve-month average daily consumption by more than 40%, and a leak is confirmed by a field visit recorded on form MT-7.

Quality Assurance Policy QA-14: Call Scoring and Complaint Rate Escalation
Version 3.2, effective 1 September 2026. Owner: Quality Assurance Team.

3. Call scoring
3.1 Each reviewed call is scored against five criteria, each out of 10. The call score is the mean of the five criteria, recorded to one decimal place.
3.2 Each agent must have at least three reviewed calls per calendar month. Where fewer are available, the monthly score is the mean of the reviewed calls only.

4. Complaint rate
4.1 The complaint rate is the number of complaints logged against an agent in a rolling 30-day period, divided by the total calls handled by that agent in the same period, expressed per 1,000 calls.

PR-SC-07.1 Scope. This section applies to all tenders for goods and services with an estimated total contract value between £10,000 and £75,000 (excluding VAT) where the requisitioning department has not requested a full open procedure.

PR-SC-07.2 Minimum response period. Bidders shall be allowed no fewer than ten (10) working days from the date of issue to submit a response. Working days exclude Saturdays, Sundays and public holidays observed in England and Wales.

PR-SC-07.3 Evaluation panel. Each panel shall have no fewer than three members, one of whom shall be the evaluation panel chair. The chair shall not have a financial interest in any bidder.

PR-SC-07.4 Scoring. Each evaluator shall score each response against the published criteria on a scale of 0 to 10. Individual scores shall be recorded to one decimal place. Where the award criterion is quality, the quality score shall be the arithmetic mean of the individual evaluator scores, rounded to two decimal places.

PR-SC-07.5 Delivery information. Bidders shall state the lead time for delivery in working days from receipt of a purchase order. Where a bidder states lead time in calendar weeks, the procurement team shall convert it at five working days per week.

PR-SC-07.6 Service history. Bidders shall provide, for the preceding twelve months, the number of service calls received and the number of scheduled visits completed. The service reliability ratio is calculated as calls received divided by scheduled visits completed.

PR-SC-07.7 Exception: urgent requirements. The response period in PR-SC-07.2 may be reduced to five (5) working days where the Director of Estates certifies in writing that a delay would expose persons or property to risk. The certificate shall be filed with the tender record.

PR-SC-07.8 Exception: sole-source. Where only one supplier can meet the specification, PR-SC-07.2 to PR-SC-07.4 do not apply. A sole-source justification form (Form PS-14) shall be approved by the Head of Procurement Operations.

7.1 A customer may request a refund of the fare paid for a journey where the scheduled service was cancelled, terminated short of the published destination, or arrived more than 25 minutes after the timetabled time.

Policy Extract: OPS-LK-07 Locker Module Faults, Service Credits and Access Rights
Document reference: OPS-LK-07 Rev 4
Issued by: Operations Standards Team, Northfield Parcel Lockers Ltd
Effective: 1 September 2026
Review date: 1 March 2027

1. Scope
1.1 This extract applies to all locker banks in the Eastern and Midlands zones, including the 12-door and 24-door modular units installed under contract LK/2019/044.
1.2 It does not cover courier-owned collection points, which are governed by OPS-LK-11.

2. Fault classification
2.1 A fault is classed as Category B where one or more doors fail to release after a valid code is entered, or where the keypad registers fewer than 90 per cent of key presses in the diagnostic cycle.
2.2 A fault is classed as Category A where a door is held open for longer than 45 seconds, or where the bank controller reports a power interruption exceeding 3 minutes.

3. Response times
3.1 Category A faults must be attended within 4 working hours of logging.
3.2 Category B faults must be attended within 1 working day of logging. Attendance is recorded when the technician scans the bank QR plate on site.

4. Service credits
4.1 A service credit of £18.50 per affected door per calendar day is payable to the network partner where a Category B fault remains open beyond the window in clause 3.2.
4.2 Credits are capped at £140.00 per bank per calendar month.
4.3 Exception: where the delay is caused by a parts backorder notified in writing to the partner before the window expires, clause 4.1 does not apply for the period of the backorder.

5. Access and keys
5.1 Technicians may open a bank cabinet only with a logged work order number.
5.2 Emergency access without a work order is permitted for Category A faults only, and must be recorded in the access log within 30 minutes.

6. Records
6.1 All attendances, parts requests and credit calculations must be entered on the field sheet and copied to the zone ledger by the end of the shift.

CASE NOTE – Bank EM-0417, Harcourt Road Retail Park
Logged by: R. Okonedo, field technician, Midlands 2
Date: 14 October 2026

Arrived 08:10 on work order WO-88213, which came in on 9 October at 16:42 as a Category B fault. The partner rep, Dan, rang twice on the way over to ask whether the bank was still down, and I said I'd know more once I'd looked at it, which is more or less what I always say. Bank has 24 doors. Doors 7, 8 and 19 would not release on a valid code. The keypad diagnostic had been run by the remote desk on the 10th, and the sheet shows 412 key presses sent against 538 registered, so I've put that down as the figure they have on file. Replaced the door solenoid on 19 and the latch harness on 7. Door 8 needed a new keypad board, which was not on the van, so I raised PR-5561 and left a note in the cabinet.

The partner later sent a message saying they had been told the parts would come on the 12th, which I could not confirm. The backorder email from stores is dated 10 October, but it was not copied to the partner's inbox, as far as I can see. Lunch was late because of the M6 closures, and I was on the bus back to the depot by 13:05. Forgot to scan the QR plate on the way out, so I went back at 13:20 and did it then.

Shift total for the week so far, per my sheet: Monday 7.5 hours, Tuesday 6.25 hours, Wednesday 8 hours, Thursday 5 hours. Parts run to be done Friday morning if PR-5561 clears.

Document ref: PS-POL-14 (Rev. 3)
Effective: 1 September 2026

Section 4: Small Tenders

4.1 A tender is classed as a small tender where the estimated total contract value, excluding VAT, is below £25,000 and the contract term does not exceed 36 months.

4.2 Small tenders may be awarded on the basis of three written quotations, provided each quotation is received through the e-Sourcing portal and carries the supplier's company registration number.

4.3 Where a single quotation is proposed, the requesting budget holder must complete Form PS-7 stating the reason no competitive quotations were obtained.

Section 5: Supplier Performance Review

5.1 Each supplier on a live framework is reviewed at the end of each quarter. Performance is measured as a service failure rate, being the number of logged service failures divided by the number of service requests raised in the quarter, expressed as a percentage.

5.2 A service failure rate of 2.0% or above in any quarter triggers a formal review under clause 5.4.

5.3 Failures attributable to the university's own timetable changes, cancelled client requests, or force majeure are excluded from the count.

5.4 A formal review shall be chaired by the Head of Procurement Services and shall conclude within 15 working days of the quarter end.

5.5 Exception: where a supplier has been reviewed under clause 5.4 in either of the two preceding quarters and the failure rate has since fallen below 2.0%, the Head of Procurement Services may, at their discretion, defer the review by one quarter and record the reason on the supplier file.

Section 6: Records

6.1 Supplier files shall be retained for six years from the date of contract expiry, in line with the university's records schedule (ref. RS-2019-044).

4.7.1 Scope
This clause applies to all sea (FCL and LCL) and road consignments booked through the Southampton and Felixstowe desks.

4.7.2 Cut-off windows
(a) A shipper must tender a full container load to the terminal no later than 16:30 on the business day before the stated vessel cut-off.
(b) Consignments tendered after 16:30 are treated as late tenders and are logged on form HV-LT/2.
(c) Road consignments collected after 14:00 on a Friday are deemed tendered on the following Monday.

4.7.3 Rebooking deadline
(a) A late tender may be rebooked onto the next available sailing provided the shipper confirms in writing within three (3) working days of the original cut-off.
(b) Working days exclude Saturdays, Sundays and English bank holidays.
(c) Confirmations received after the third working day lapse and the booking is closed.

4.7.4 Exception: documented port delay

7.2.2 Head injuries must be recorded as a separate entry and the parent or carer informed by telephone within 15 minutes of the incident being identified.

7.3.1 Prescription medicine may be administered only where a signed Medication Consent Form has been received and the dose has been checked against the label by two members of staff.

7. Temperature excursions

7.1 A temperature excursion is any period during which product temperature, as recorded by a calibrated logger in the load or at the dock probe point, is outside its storage band for longer than the tolerance in clause 7.3.

7.2 Loggers shall record at intervals not exceeding 10 minutes. Logger serial numbers are recorded on the Load Release Sheet (Form HCL-LRS-3).

7.3 Tolerance. Chilled product may remain above +5 C for up to 45 minutes cumulative per load. Frozen product may not exceed -15 C for any period.

7.4 Each excursion shall be logged in the Excursion Register within one working hour of detection, stating the logger ID, start time, end time, peak reading and the duty manager's name.

7.5 Any load with an excursion over tolerance is placed on QA hold. The load shall not be released until a disposition is recorded by a QA technician.

7.6 Exception: dock door events. Where an excursion occurs solely because a dock door is open during loading or unloading, and the total open time does not exceed 20 minutes, the excursion is excluded from the tolerance in clause 7.3 provided that the door-open event is recorded on the dock log (Form HCL-DL-1) with a signature from the shift supervisor. The exclusion does not apply to weekend or bank-holiday operations unless a second signature from the on-call QA technician is also obtained.

7.7 Carrier units without a recording logger are not eligible for release under any exception in this clause.

7.8 Dispositions are recorded as RELEASE, DOWNGRADE or DESTROY. Dispositions of DESTROY require countersignature by the Head of Quality Assurance or deputy.

Revision history: Rev 3 (14 March 2025) amended 7.3 from 30 to 45 minutes. Rev 4 added 7.6.

Repeat Attendance, Re-triage and Results Follow-Up

7. Repeat attendance

7.1 A patient returning within 72 hours of a previous attendance for the same presenting complaint must be reviewed by a clinician before discharge, not by the triage nurse alone.

Dispensing & Prescription Collection Policy
Document ref: DCP-07 (rev. 4)
Owner: Responsible Pharmacist, Dispensing Desk
Effective: 1 September 2026
Review date: 1 March 2027

1. Scope
1.1 This policy applies to all NHS and private prescriptions presented at the collection desk, including repeat dispensing items and owing slips.
1.2 Staff must read this policy alongside SOP-14 (Controlled Drugs Register) and the Medicines Storage Procedure, ref. MSP-03.

2. Ready-for-collection holding period
2.1 Dispensed items are held in the bagged-prescription bay for a maximum of 14 days from the date of dispensing.
2.2 Items not collected within that period are returned to stock, and the pharmacy record is annotated "not collected – returned" with the initials of the member of staff who processed the return.
2.3 Items containing Schedule 2 or Schedule 3 controlled drugs are held for 7 days only and are then returned to the dispensary for destruction checks.

3. Identity and authority to collect
3.1 The patient, or a named nominee recorded on the patient profile, must collect the medicine. Staff must check date of birth or photo identification before handing over any Schedule 2 or Schedule 3 item.
3.2 Collection by a third party who is not a recorded nominee requires the responsible pharmacist's approval and a signed authorisation form (Form CD-9b).

4. Exceptions
4.1 Where a patient is admitted to hospital or is housebound, the responsible pharmacist may extend the holding period for a non-controlled item by up to 21 days, provided the extension is noted on the bag label and the pharmacy record.
4.2 An extension under clause 4.1 does not apply to Schedule 2 or Schedule 3 items, which remain subject to clause 2.3 in all cases.
4.3 Any extension must be recorded with the date of the extension, the reason given, and the name of the person who authorised it.

5. Recording
5.1 Each collection is recorded on the dispensing system with the date, time, and collector's name. Times are entered in 24-hour format.
5.2 Discrepancies between the bag label and the register must be reported to the responsible pharmacist before the item is released.

Customer Billing Policy BP-14: Estimated Bills, Meter Readings and Back-Billing
Version 3.2 | Effective 1 September 2026 | Owner: Customer Billing Team, Leeds

1. Scope
1.1 This policy applies to all domestic and small business accounts billed on a monthly or quarterly cycle.

2. Meter readings
2.1 Customers should submit a meter reading through the online portal or the automated phone line between the 20th and the last day of each billing month.
2.2 Where no actual reading has been received for 90 days or more, the billing system will issue an estimated bill.
2.3 An estimated bill must not exceed the customer's average daily consumption over the previous 12 months multiplied by the number of days in the billing period.

3. Back-billing
3.1 Where an actual reading shows consumption above the amount billed, the difference may be back-billed for up to 12 months from the date of the reading.
3.2 Back-billed amounts above £300.00 must be approved by a Billing Team Leader before issue.
3.3 Customers must be offered a payment plan of no fewer than 6 and no more than 18 monthly instalments.

4. Exceptions
4.1 Clause 3.1 does not apply where the supplier failed to obtain a reading for reasons attributable to the supplier, including a reader appointment cancelled by the supplier.

AP-POL-07 Rev. 3: Goods Receipt Variance and Invoice Hold Procedure
Effective 1 March 2026. Approved by: R. Okonedo, Financial Controller

7.1 Purpose
This clause sets out how Accounts Payable treats supplier invoices where the invoiced quantity or value differs from the goods receipt note (GRN) or purchase order (PO).

7.2 Tolerance
Invoices within a variance of 2.0% of PO value, or £150.00, whichever is the lower, may be approved by the AP Team Leader without further reference.

7.3 Hold
Any invoice outside the tolerance in 7.2 is placed on hold (status HOLD-VAR) and referred to the budget holder named on the PO.

7.4 Exception: Consignment Stock
Where the supplier is recorded on the Vendor Master with consignment flag = Y, variance tolerance in 7.2 does not apply. Invoices are matched to the consumption report issued under SC-CONS-02 and released on the first working day after receipt of that report.

7.5 Exception: Expedited Freight
Freight invoices raised against a PO marked EXPEDITE are exempt from 7.3 where the approving director has signed the expedite authorisation form (FORM AP-EX-2). The form reference must be recorded in the PO notes field.

7.6 Time Limit
Held invoices must be resolved within 10 working days of the hold date. Items unresolved after this period are escalated to the Financial Controller.

3.1 Every delivered assignment is scored by the quality reviewer against the Meridian Scoring Sheet (MSS-2) within five working days of delivery. A score of 88 or above on a 100-point scale is recorded as accepted.

Section 3: Leak allowance eligibility

3.1 A leak allowance may be considered where a customer reports a suspected concealed leak on the customer-side supply pipe and the leak is confirmed by a Harrowmere field engineer.

3.2 The allowance is calculated on the excess consumption above the customer's baseline. The baseline is the mean daily consumption for the 90 days preceding the reported leak, expressed in cubic metres (m³), rounded to two decimal places.

3.3 The excess consumption is the difference between the metered reading at the date of repair and the metered reading at the date the leak was first reported, less the baseline multiplied by the number of days between those two dates.

3.4 Allowances are credited at the tariff rate of £1.84 per m³ in effect on the date the repair is confirmed. Credits below £5.00 are not issued and are carried to the next billing cycle.

3.5 Where the reported leak is confirmed to be on the Harrowmere-owned communication pipe, no allowance is payable under this section.

Section 4: Exceptions

4.1 Clause 3.2 does not apply to customers registered on the Priority Services Register, for whom the baseline shall be set at 0.35 m³ per day regardless of the 90-day mean.

4.2 Where a repair visit is delayed beyond 5 working days by reason of Harrowmere access failure, the reporting date shall be taken as the date of the first failed visit, not the date of the original report.

4.3 Allowances exceeding 180 kg of recovered water equivalent (as recorded on Form LA-7) require sign-off by the Billing Adviser before credit. Forms weighing more than 2 lb in printed copy are to be scanned rather than posted.

7. Discharge readiness criteria
7.1 A patient is recorded as medically fit for discharge (MFD) only when the responsible consultant has documented the MFD decision in the EPR discharge summary template (form DS-14).

7.3 Where a community package of care is required, the referral must be logged with the Integrated Care Hub no later than 48 hours before the planned discharge date.

8. Medicines reconciliation
8.1 Discharge medicines must be reconciled by a pharmacist or a prescriber trained in reconciliation before the patient leaves the ward.
8.2 At least 90% of discharge medicine lines must carry a reconciled status at the point of discharge. Wards below this threshold shall be reported to the Medicines Safety Group on the next working day.

9. Escalation
9.1 Any patient who remains an inpatient for more than 72 hours after the MFD date shall be listed on the daily Delayed Discharge Register (form BM-22).
9.2 Exception: where a patient is awaiting a bed on a specialist unit, the 72-hour period is measured from the date the specialist bed was confirmed, not from the MFD date. The ward sister must record the bed reference in the register comments field.
9.3 Exception: patients receiving end-of-life care under the Hospice-at-Home pathway are not subject to clause 9.1 and are reviewed weekly by the Palliative Care Lead.

10. Family and carer engagement
10.1 Discharge planning meetings shall be held where the patient or carer has requested one, and attendance shall be recorded on form DS-15.
10.2 Carer feedback scores on the post-discharge telephone survey are reported as a mean of the individual scores recorded for each ward in the quarter.

4.1.1 This section sets out the approval levels, matching requirements and exception handling that apply to supplier invoices received at the Stockport and Wakefield sites.

4.2.1 Invoices up to and including GBP 4,999.99 may be approved by a Team Leader, AP.

4.3.1 Each invoice shall be matched to a purchase order and a goods received note (GRN) before payment is released.

4.4.1 Bulk steel supplier invoices are matched on net weight recorded at the weighbridge, in kilograms (kg).
4.4.2 Where the weighbridge ticket is in pounds (lb), the clerk shall convert at 1 lb = 0.4536 kg before matching.
4.4.3 Freight charges are accepted up to 6.5 hours of driver time per load, or the equivalent recorded in the carrier's log.

4.5.1 Clause 4.2.2 does not apply to invoices from suppliers on the Approved Consignment List (ACL) where a standing approval reference is recorded on the PO. Such invoices may be approved by a Team Leader, AP up to GBP 9,999.99.

Revision 3 | Effective 1 September 2026 | Owner: Operations Manager

1. Scope
1.1 This policy applies to all sea and road consignments booked under a Halvorsen tariff, including part loads and consolidated LCL shipments.

2. Definitions
2.1 "Declared weight" means the gross weight entered on the booking at confirmation.
2.2 "Verified weight" means the weight recorded on the origin weighbridge ticket or terminal gate weight.
2.3 "Variance" means verified weight less declared weight, expressed in kilograms.

3. Re-rating
3.1 Where variance exceeds 250 kg, the booking shall be re-rated at the applicable tariff band.
3.2 Re-rating shall be notified to the shipper within one (1) working day of receipt of the verified weight.

4.2 Consignments under the Priority Road service (ref. PRS-2) are excluded from clause 3.1 where the shipper has accepted the flat-rate surcharge of GBP 85.00.

4. Sickness absence reporting and entitlement

4.1 Employees must notify their line manager by telephone or Teams call no later than 09:30 on the first day of absence. Messages sent by email or text do not count as notification unless the manager has confirmed receipt.

4.4 Absence of fewer than 4 consecutive calendar days does not require a fit note. Absence of 4 or more consecutive calendar days requires a fit note from a registered GP or medical practitioner, to be sent to the People Team within 5 working days of the first day of absence.

5. Absence management thresholds

5.1 The absence trigger points for formal review are as follows:
(a) 5 or more separate episodes in a rolling 12-month period;
(b) 14 or more total days lost in a rolling 12-month period;
(c) any single absence exceeding 21 consecutive calendar days.

5.2 Where two or more triggers in clause 5.1 apply at the same review date, the case is escalated to the Operations Director for review under clause 6.

5.3 Days lost are counted as working days scheduled to be worked, excluding bank holidays and approved leave. Part-days are counted as half a day for each part-day episode.

6. Exceptions

6.1 Clauses 5.1(a) and 5.1(b) shall not apply to absence that is wholly related to a disability recognised under the Equality Act 2010, provided that the employee has consented to the disclosure of an occupational health report to the People Team.

6.2 The Operations Director may, at their discretion, disregard up to 2 episodes in a rolling 12-month period where the episodes are linked to a single diagnosed condition and the employee is following a documented treatment plan.

**RSP-14: Refunds and Fare Adjustments**
Version 3.2. Effective 2 October 2026. Owner: Rider Support Operations, Northgate office.

**1. Scope**

1.1 This policy applies to refund requests from riders where the charged fare differs from the metered fare recorded in the trip ledger.

1.2 Agents must not promise a refund before the trip record has been reviewed.

**2. Eligibility**

2.1 A refund may be issued where the charged fare exceeds the metered fare by more than £2.00.

2.2 A claim must be lodged within 14 days of the trip end timestamp. The trip end timestamp is the dropoff time recorded by the driver app, converted to local time.

2.3 Fare components are assessed separately: base fare, distance charge, time charge, booking fee, surcharges and waiting fees.

**3. Waiting fees**

3.1 Waiting time is chargeable only after the free waiting allowance has elapsed. The allowance is 4 minutes.
*Revision note: 3.1 previously read "5 minutes". Corrected 9 October 2026 following Pricing Ticket PT-2291.*

3.2 Waiting fees are charged at £0.30 per minute, rounded down to the whole minute.

**4. Exceptions**

4.1 Clause 2.2 does not apply where the driver has logged a safety incident against the trip. In those cases the claim window is 30 days from the trip end timestamp.

4.2 Where a trip was booked as a multi-stop journey, each stop is assessed under clause 2.3 as a separate line, and the booking fee is not refundable in part.

**5. Evidence**

5.1 Where a rider disputes a waiting fee, the driver's arrival photograph and location trace are the primary evidence. Agents must confirm that the photo set is complete. A complete set is the number of photographs listed in the booking record.

Section 7: Temperature Excursions and Load Release
Policy Extract CC-7.3 (Rev. 4, effective 1 September 2026)

7.3.1 Scope
This clause applies to all chilled (0°C to +5°C) and frozen (−18°C or below) loads leaving the Hadleigh and Wrexham cross-dock sites, including multi-drop vehicles.

7.3.2 Probe readings
Each load shall be probed at dispatch using a calibrated probe thermometer. The core reading shall be recorded on the Dispatch Release Sheet (form DRS-2) in the "Core °C" field. Readings taken from the vehicle air supply are not acceptable as a core reading.

7.3.3 Excursion threshold
A load is in excursion when any product core reading exceeds its band by more than 2.0°C for a cumulative period of 30 minutes or longer. Cumulative time shall be logged from the data logger in hours and minutes (hh:mm), not as decimal hours.

7.3.4 Dispatcher action on excursion
Where an excursion is identified before departure, the dispatcher shall:
(a) place the load on hold in WMS status "QA-HOLD";
(b) notify the Duty Quality Officer within 15 minutes of identification;
(c) not release the load until a written disposition is recorded on DRS-2.

7.3.5 Exception: short-term excursion on frozen stock
Frozen loads may be released without QA-HOLD where the core reading is no higher than −15°C, the cumulative excursion is less than 45 minutes, and the Duty Quality Officer has approved release by telephone. Approval shall be recorded on DRS-2 with the officer's staff number.

7.3.6 Exception does not apply to
(a) chilled loads containing raw poultry, minced meat or shellfish;
(b) loads carrying a customer temperature certificate;
(c) any load where the data logger has failed or shows gaps longer than 10 minutes.

7.3.7 Record retention
DRS-2 forms and data logger downloads shall be retained for 36 months from the date of dispatch.

BA-7.1 Scope
This section applies to annual and monthly subscriptions to the Brightwater Pro, Brightwater Team and Brightwater Enterprise plans, billed in GBP, EUR or USD.

BA-7.2 Service credit eligibility
A customer is eligible for a service credit where a verified service incident has lasted longer than 4 consecutive hours within the billing period and the incident is recorded in the Status Register under a reference beginning SR-.

BA-7.3 Credit calculation
The credit equals the pro-rata monthly fee for the affected seats multiplied by 0.05 for each full 4-hour block beyond the first, up to a maximum of 0.25 of the monthly fee. Credits are rounded down to the nearest penny.

BA-7.4 Dispute window
A customer may raise a subscription dispute within 15 working days of the invoice date. Working days exclude Saturdays, Sundays and English bank holidays. The Account Manager must acknowledge the dispute within 2 working days of receipt.

BA-7.5 Refund approval
Refunds up to £500.00 may be approved by an Account Manager. Refunds above £500.00 and up to £2,500.00 require approval from the Billing Operations Lead. Refunds above £2,500.00 require approval from the Finance Director.

BA-7.6 Exception: prior written waiver
Notwithstanding BA-7.4, a dispute raised after the window closes shall be accepted where the customer holds a written waiver issued under Form BA-F9 by a Billing Operations Lead and the waiver is dated within the 90 calendar days preceding the invoice date. Waivers issued by any other role are not valid for this purpose.

BA-7.7 Record keeping
All credit and refund decisions must be logged in the Billing Ledger with the Status Register reference, the invoice number and the approving role.

7. Recording and counting of landed weight

7.1 Every landing of quota-managed species shall be recorded on a landing slip (Form LS-4) at the time of weighing. Each slip shall show vessel registration, member number, date, species, net weight in kilograms, and the scale identifier.

7.2 The landed weight for a trip is the sum of the net weights on all LS-4 slips raised for that trip, including replacement slips issued under clause 7.4.

7.3 Landed weight is counted against the member's annual allocation as held on the date of landing. Where cumulative landed weight would exceed that allocation, the Landing Officer shall place the vessel on hold and notify the Quota Secretary the same working day.

7.4 Where the landing scale reading differs from the buyer's weighbridge by more than 0.5 kg per 100 kg, the buyer's weighbridge figure applies and a replacement slip shall be raised marked "RE-WEIGH".

7.5 Exception, swapped tonnage. Tonnage received under a swap agreement approved by the Board before the landing date may be added to the allocation for that landing only, provided the swap reference is entered in box 9 of the slip. Swap references take the form SW-2026/nnn.

7.6 Exception, distress landings. Landings made under a distress notice (Form DN-1) shall be recorded and weighed as normal but shall not be counted against allocation until the Board has reviewed the notice. The DN-1 reference shall be entered in box 10 of the slip.

7.7 Scale checks shall be logged on Form SC-2 at the start of each landing day, recording each test-weight reading in kilograms.

Preamble. Most of the refund questions that reach the box office are simple, and this section is meant to keep them simple. It is also the section people reach for when a patron has had a bad evening, so please read it all the way through before you quote anybody a number. Yes, the clauses below are a little long. Ruth asked for them to be written out in full after the spring incident with the Tuesday matinee, and nobody has found a shorter way of saying it that doesn't leave a gap somewhere.

4.1 Standard refund window. A patron may request a refund on a ticket for a performance up to and including 48 hours before its start time, subject to clause 4.3.

4.2 Processing fee. A non-refundable booking fee of £2.50 per ticket applies to all refunds. Group bookings of ten or more are charged the fee once per booking, not per seat, as agreed with the Harbourside Group Sales team in January.

4.3 Late requests and exceptions. Requests made less than 48 hours before the performance may be refunded at the discretion of the duty House Manager only where one or more of the following applies: (a) the performance was cancelled or materially altered by the Playhouse; (b) the patron has a medical certificate dated within seven days of the performance; (c) the patron is a bereaved next-of-kin, on production of evidence to the satisfaction of the duty House Manager. Exceptions under (a) do not attract the fee in clause 4.2.

4.4 Accessibility seating. Wheelchair and companion bookings are refunded in full, including the fee, at any time, on the Access Team's confirmation.

4.5 Vouchers. Where a refund is declined under clause 4.3, the patron may be offered a Playhouse credit voucher equal to the ticket face value less the fee. Vouchers expire 12 months from issue, are non-transferable, and are not cash-convertible.

Case note (BO/2026/0917), prepared by Dev Chaudhry, Box Office Supervisor, 22 October 2026.

Mr Okonkwo-Reyes rang the box office at 09:14 on Monday 19 October, and again at 10:02, to say his daughter had come down with a stomach bug and would not be fit to attend the Saturday 24 October 19:30 performance of "The Glass Orchard". He held four tickets in Row G, seats 11 to 14, booked on 2 October for a total of £168.00 (four tickets at £42.00 each). He had been told at the time of booking that the fee applied. He also mentioned, in the middle of a long call about parking, that his mother-in-law had been moved to a hospice in Ashford the same week and that the family had been "running about all weekend", which is why he hadn't rung sooner. He asked whether we could return the money in full.

I explained clause 4.1 and that the request fell inside 48 hours. He said he understood, but asked whether a sick child counted as medical. I told him I would check with the duty House Manager. The House Manager on Monday was Keisha Lund; she said a medical certificate would be needed under 4.3(b) and that the bereavement point under 4.3(c) did not appear to apply to the hospice admission as described.

The patron has since emailed a photograph of a GP letter dated 20 October, addressed to his daughter, which describes a gastrointestinal illness and advises her to rest for five days. The letter is dated after the performance was missed and was not sent in before it. Three other patrons from the same booking have not yet been contacted.

Status at time of writing: awaiting decision from the duty House Manager. Patron has been told that a decision will follow within five working days.

SOP-CO-014 v3.2 – Visit Windows, Sample Handling and Deviations
Effective 1 March 2026. Controlled copy: site file, binder section 4.

4.1 Scope
This procedure applies to all scheduled study visits for protocol RCU-LM-22 (Study Lipid Modulation, Phase II) and to all biological samples collected at those visits.

4.2 Visit windows
4.2.1 Each scheduled visit has a target day and a window expressed as days from Day 1 (randomisation).
4.2.2 Visits outside the window are recorded as protocol deviations and reported to the sponsor within 5 working days.
4.2.3 Visits may be rescheduled by the coordinator only within the window. Any change to the target day requires written approval from the principal investigator (PI).

4.3 Sample collection and processing
4.3.1 Fasting bloods must be drawn between 07:30 and 09:00. Samples drawn outside this range are labelled "non-fasting" on the requisition.
4.3.2 Serum tubes are allowed to clot for 30 minutes before centrifugation at 1,500 g for 10 minutes.
4.3.3 Samples must be placed in the −80 °C freezer within 90 minutes of collection.

4.4 Exceptions
4.4.1 Where a participant's visit falls outside the window because of a documented illness, the PI may approve a visit up to 7 days beyond the upper limit. Approval must be recorded on form RCU-F-09 before the visit takes place.
4.4.2 Samples held beyond 90 minutes at room temperature because of equipment failure may be retained if the freezer log and the courier manifest are both filed with the sample record.

Case note – CN-2026-031

Visit 4 took place on Day 96. The participant reported a chest infection on Day 80 and attended a GP appointment on Day 81, a copy of which is in the source file. Riverside Lane Pharmacy: Dispensing and Collection Desk

**Policy DCD/04: Held and Uncollected Prescriptions**
Version 3.2, effective 1 September 2026. Ref: RLP-POL-DCD-04

4.1 Prescriptions dispensed but not collected within 14 calendar days of being marked "ready" are returned to the held shelf for return to stock, subject to clauses 4.4 and 4.5.

4.2 Before any return to stock, the dispensing technician must confirm that the patient has been contacted at least twice by telephone or SMS. Each attempt is recorded on the PMR under the "Contact log" tab, with date, time, method and initials.

4.3 Controlled drugs (Schedule 2 and Schedule 3 CD) must not be returned to stock under this policy. They are destroyed under DCD/09 after 28 days.

4.4 Exception: where the patient is a care-home resident, or the prescription contains a cold-chain item, the 14-day period is extended to 21 calendar days. This applies only if the item has been stored at 2 to 8°C throughout and the fridge log shows no out-of-range reading since dispensing. Fridge readings must be taken at least three times daily and recorded.

4.5 Where the prescriber has annotated the prescription "do not return", the item remains held until a pharmacist authorises disposal in writing.

**Case note, 19 October 2026, entered by A. Mensah (DT)**

Mrs P. Kowalczyk's insulin pen and needles were marked ready on 9 October. Her date of birth is blank on the PMR because the registration form was never scanned back in, so I have only matched her by name and postcode. Her daughter rang on the 12th to say she is in respite until the end of the month, which I put in the notes but did not confirm with the care home. I sent six SMS reminders between the 12th and the 18th; the system shows 38 reminders sent across the whole week, and 9 came back as undelivered. Two calls went unanswered on the 16th and 17th, logged as attempts one and two. The fridge in the dispensary was propped open for six minutes on the 15th while the wholesaler delivery was unpacked, and the 17th reading was 5.1°C, with 3.8°C at 08:45 and 4.4°C on the 18th. Nobody has written down what the fridge did between the 15th and the 17th. The prescription has no "do not return" annotation.

criteria: Mid: average at least 3.0°C but below 6.0°C

criteria: Moderate: at least 10% but below 24% undelivered

Document ref: QA-POL-07, Revision 4, effective 1 September 2026

7. TEMPERATURE EXCURSIONS

7.1 Chilled product (setpoint 2°C to 8°C) is rejected at receipt if the probe reading exceeds 8.0°C at the time of unloading.

7.2 Frozen product (setpoint −18°C or colder) is held in quarantine if any logged reading is warmer than −15.0°C for more than 30 consecutive minutes.

7.3 Any excursion recorded under 7.1 or 7.2 is reported to the Quality Duty Officer within 2 working days of the event. Working days exclude Saturdays, Sundays and bank holidays observed in England.

7.4 Quarantined stock is assessed by the Quality Duty Officer and released, downgraded or destroyed under form QA-F-22 (Disposition Record).

7.5 Exception: where a carrier's own data logger shows the reading was within limits for the full transit period and the depot probe was faulty, the Quality Duty Officer may release the load under 7.2 with a countersigned calibration certificate dated no more than 90 days before the event.

7.6 Probe calibration references are recorded against the unit on the fleet register. A probe failing its ice-point check (0.0°C ± 0.5°C) is removed from service.

The carrier's data logger (serial CL-0882-B) shows chilled readings between 3.2°C and 5.0°C for the full transit, and frozen readings between −19.1°C and −17.6°C, with a single entry at 05:58 of −14.2°C recorded during fuelling.

Depot probe TH-P-09 last passed its ice-point check on 2 October 2026 (reading 0.2°C). Probe TH-P-09 was not re-checked after a battery change on 12 October.

Chilled pallets were rejected at 06:24. Frozen pallets are on hold in bay 4, pending disposition. Carrier driver T. Nwachukwu has been asked for the logger download and calibration certificate for the unit in use.
